tags.name: MSP
tags.description: MSP APIs to get and manage tenants related information.

get.summary: Get a device inventory list across managed tenants
get.description: This API endpoint retrieves a list of network devices in inventory across all tenants managed by a Managed Service Provider (MSP), such as access points, switches, and gateways. The API includes devices that are yet to be onboarded, as well as those already onboarded and currently being monitored by the system. In addition to the standard device details such as serial number, device name, part number, deployment, device function, scope ID, device group ID, and provisioning status, each device in the returned list also includes the identifier and name of the tenant that owns the device. The query parameters allow you to narrow down the results to devices that meet specific criteria, ensuring you receive only the relevant data.

This API provides the list of tenants for an MSP. Tenants list includes details like tenant name, tenant CID, sites count, devices count with health status, alerts count, etc. The query parameters allow you to narrow down the results that meet specific criteria, ensuring you receive only the relevant data.

**Deprecated:** This operation is deprecated in favor of `GET /network-msp/v2/list-tenants`. Please migrate to the v2 endpoint before the sunset date indicated in the `Sunset` response header.

get.summary: Get paginated list of MSP subscription keys
get.description: Returns a paginated list of MSP subscription keys with tier type, expiry date, subscribed customer count, order ID, and PO number. Results are sorted by subscribed customers (descending). Query time is always the current time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of subscription items to return per page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based offset for pagination. Defaults to 0.

Filter.name: filter
Filter.description:
OData Version 4.0 filter string (limited functionality). Supports only 'and' conjunction ('or' and 'not' are NOT supported). Supported fields and operators are in the below given table.
| Field | Operators |
| ----------------- | ---- |
| `tenantName`    | `eq` |
| `deviceOwnership` | `in` |

**The operators are implemented as follows:**

* `eq`: Only values exactly matching the given value are returned.

* `in`: Only values present in the given list are returned.

**Using Special Character for filtering the `tenantName`**

* If the `tenantName` needs to be filtered with a special character like a single quote `'`, then it has to be passed as escaped character.

* For example: `tenantName eq 'Tenant\\'s account 1'`
Filter.example: tenantName eq 'tenant A' and deviceOwnership in ('MSP', 'TENANT')

Sort.name: sort
Sort.description:
Sorting can be supported on the following fields: `tenantName`, `totalSites`, `deviceHealthStatus`, `degradedSites`, `alerts`, `deviceOwnership` and `createdTime`.

For `alerts`, sorting will be done in order of `critical`, `major` and `minor` counts. For example if input is `alerts DESC`, then the tenant row with the highest `critical` alerts count will appear at the top.

For `deviceHealthStatus` sorting will be done in order of `poor`, `fair` and `good` counts. For example if input is `deviceHealthStatus DESC`, then the tenant row with the highest `poor` health count will appear at the top.

SortMspDeviceInventory.name: sort
SortMspDeviceInventory.description:
A comma-separated list of sort expressions. Each sort expression is a property name optionally followed by a direction indicator asc (ascending) or desc (descending).

The first sort expression in the list defines the primary sort order, the second defines the secondary sort order, and so on. If a direction indicator is omitted the default direction is ascending.
Supported fields are `tenantId`, `tenantName`, `siteId`, `siteName`, `serialNumber`, `deviceName`, `deviceType`, `ipv4`, `model`, `deviceGroupName`, and `deviceFunction`.

Sortmsp.name: sort
Sortmsp.description:

For `deviceHealthStatus` sorting will be done in order of `poor`, `fair` and `good` counts. For example if input is `deviceHealthStatus DESC`, then the tenant row with the highest `poor` health count will appear at the top.
